evidence: STATIC: task/solution/solve.sh (sha256 f7c17a01...be2e) is 5 lines: '#!/bin/bash', 'set -euo pipefail', 'mkdir -p /app', 'cp -a "$(dirname "$0")/app/." /app/'. Byte-identical to the frozen template solve.sh (cmp). LF only (0 CR bytes, od -c), bash -n OK, writes only /app, nothing to /tests, /logs/verifier or /solution, no pkill, no NODE_ENV, no network fetch or install (also satisfies the stricter Internal sheet wording). Shipped tree: package.json, server.js, public/{app.js,index.html,styles.css,transcript.css}, seed/seed_data.json; no app.db, no node_modules, no symlinks (find -type l empty), matching integration.md L5 ('hand it over without a database', 'no symbolic links'). Seed copy is byte-identical to environment/assets/seed_data.json (sha256 f69616e2...be36), satisfying 'Copy /assets/seed_data.json into /app'. server.js: L14 DB_PATH = process.env.DB_PATH || path.join(__dirname,'app.db'); L15/L29 files resolved via __dirname (cwd-independent, integration.md L3); L42 /api/health registered before DB-gated middleware and always 200; L71-80 init() wraps open/seed/sweep in try/catch so health stays up on DB failure; L94 seedDatabase returns early on settings.seeded and the whole import is one transaction (L95-127), so seeding is idempotent; L519 listens on 0.0.0.0:PORT (PORT defaults to 3000; test.sh injects 3000); CLOCK taken from seed.clock (2026-05-12T11:00:00Z). Runtime deps express@5.1.0/better-sqlite3@12.4.1 match package.json and are global in both environment/Dockerfile L9-11 and tests/Dockerfile L16-21 (NODE_PATH). node --check server.js OK. RUNTIME (this review, 2026-10-09, fresh images built from the frozen environment/ and tests/ Dockerfiles, tags qc-r3-row19-kittle-agent:tmp / qc-r3-row19-kittle-verifier:tmp, own container names, removed afterwards): ran 'bash /solution/solve.sh' in the agent image (exit 0, /app populated, no db); tarred /app and /assets into the verifier image (environment_mode=separate) and replayed test.sh L72-112 (symlink scan, chown 65534, writable check passed so APP_ENTRY=/app/server.js, setsid env -i PATH/NODE_PATH/HOME/PORT=3000/DB_PATH=/app/app.db setpriv uid 65534, cwd /). Results: GET /api/health 200 {ok:true,booted:true,clock:2026-05-12T11:00:00Z}; anonymous GET /api/matters 401; GET / 200; POST /api/session harriet@kittle.test/password123 200 partner; GET /api/matters 200 with M-11..; POST /api/matters/M-11/messages 201 K-18; search finds it. Killed the process group and relaunched on the same DB: K-18 still found, sqlite shows users=5, messages=18, seeded='1' (no reimport). Alternative DB_PATH=/tmp/alt/x.db: fresh seeded DB created at that path (x.db, -wal, -shm), probe absent there, so DB_PATH is honoured. DB_PATH=/root/x.db and DB_PATH=/app (directory) as uid 65534: log 'Database initialisation failed: unable to open database file', yet /api/health 200 {booted:false}. PRIOR EVIDENCE: raw-evidence-index entries re-hashed: run_golden.sh b61aa378..., golden-run.log 4da6ab5d... match; its matching_source_files hashes all equal the frozen task bytes; the log shows the frozen solve.sh installing the golden, uid 65534/env -i/cwd /tmp launch, 18 scripted checks PASS before and after a real kill/restart (pids 28->57). That run used cw-editor-agent-r3 rather than this task's image; my run above closes that gap with images built from the frozen Dockerfiles. COUNTER-PROBES: a plausible broken reference that could pass a source-only read (DB path hard-coded to cwd, or seeding re-run every start, or health behind the DB middleware) is ruled out by the restart/alt-path/unopenable-DB runs above. A conforming alternative (seed at /app/seed_data.json, or reading /assets directly) is not penalised by this row; server.js itself accepts both locations (L29). Scope note: this row does not measure full test.sh+RewardKit grading, Oracle or model scores (rows 21/22/workload). Non-contractual observation: DB_PATH under /proc (e.g. /proc/forbidden/x.db) makes node hang before listen (fs.mkdirSync recursive under procfs), so health is not served; the harness only ever passes /app/app.db or /tmp/submission/app.db, so this is not a contract defect.
